title: Leo Knox | Curious, independent, and here for the interesting bits
desc: Meet Leo Knox: curious, independent, and hands-on. Technology, Minecraft, visual experiences, cities, AI, fitness, coffee, and how I make sense of the world.
hero:
Hi, I’m Leo.
I take things seriously.
And have fun with them.
intro:
I ask why, then like to try things for myself.
Facts and logic matter to me. So do games, good jokes, and new experiences.
down: Scroll down. Get to know me.
caption: This page, like me, is still taking shape.
personintro:
Sometimes I follow a question all the way down.
Sometimes I just want to see how far a ridiculous idea can go.
traits: Knowing what something is rarely feels like the end. I explore, experiment, look at the results, and adjust what I think.
A good answer still needs evidence.
An answer from an authority or an AI is still worth checking. I want to know what is fact, what is inference, and what is a guess.
Serious about details. Open to absurdity.
I like memes, teasing, and ideas that go a little off the rails. Careful thinking and a sense of humor belong in the same room.
mindhead:
I care about
how a conclusion holds up.
mindintro:
I put individual problems back into their systems, look for causes, and leave room for new evidence.
Thinking is a loop, rather than a verdict.
mindnote: Separate facts from opinions. Look for root causes. Change the judgment when the evidence changes.
habitintro:
I tinker with tools, notice patterns,
and make room for small experiences.
habits: I like keeping useful data and the steps that matter, comparing changes over time, and looking for the longer pattern.
Make my tools work my way.
I enjoy configuring and reshaping my digital environment. Transparency, flexibility, and having a choice matter to me.
I record training and pay attention to how I feel. Beyond the gym, I also make small adjustments to find what works for me.
Leave room for things that are just interesting.
Coffee I enjoy, a beautiful video, or a good conversation can make a day better. They do not need a grand justification.
interestintro:
Some interests start with a question. Others start with an experience.
The discoveries along the way keep me interested.
interests: From network protocols to operating systems, servers, and security, I like understanding the mechanisms—and building and testing things myself.
What can it do? And how does it work?
I enjoy the freedom to explore and create in Minecraft, along with the interactions, communities, and players from different language backgrounds.
There is a world to explore, and people to share it with.
Displays, HDR, high refresh rates, hardware, and the feel of a system catch my attention. Specs help, but I still want to see the result for myself.
Sometimes a beautiful image is its own reward.
I enjoy different cities and environments, noticing transport, infrastructure, public services, and ways of living. Travel is also a way of understanding how the world works.
Look at the view. Then look at how the city runs.
I use AI, but I also question its limits, reasoning, and mistakes. It is both a collaborator and something I want to understand better.
Embrace the tool. Keep the judgment.
An everyday event can lead me into a conversation about history, institutions, incentives, or behavior. Memes and wildly exaggerated ideas have a place too.
A conversation can go deep—or get delightfully weird.
Training, records, and observation help me understand how I am doing. I like having data alongside my own impressions when I look for progress.
Notice what changed. Adjust the next step.
Coffee that tastes right, a relaxed but interesting conversation, or a sudden idea can make an ordinary day more enjoyable.
Small things are worth paying attention to.
principlehead:
A few things
I want to hold on to.
principleintro: Less of a manifesto. More of a reminder when making choices.
principles: Understand what happened before deciding how to judge it.
Popularity and authority do not replace thinking.
Test what can be tested. Be honest about what remains unknown.
Value open technology, the exchange of information, and digital autonomy.
Acknowledge the mistake, understand its cause, and use the feedback.
Care about responsiveness, keeping my word, and conversations with substance.
Let technology serve a real need
Consider cost, stability, and results. Complexity needs a reason.
notecaption: Explore the world. Leave a little room for imagination.
contacthead:
Getting to know someone
can start with hello.
contactintro:
A point of view, something funny,
or just a hello. All welcome.
footer: A small corner of the internet, by Leo.
